questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Riders should stay close together while leaving space to move safely. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated.

questions.question: When stopping, it is best to:

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: Apply brakes smoothly and firmly. Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line while braking.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do one action at a time. Do not brake and swerve together because this may cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, you should:

options.text: Alternate between your headlight's low and high beam settings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks for any reason.
Try to cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks at a 45-degree angle or steeper. Then make a quick, sharp turn. If you go slowly or at a shallow angle, the tracks can catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed in addition to a helmet.
Not needed if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing even with a helmet. Hearing protection lets you hear important sounds like horns and sirens while protecting your ears.

questions.question: When exiting a highway while riding in a group, which formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or exiting a highway. Use staggered formation for normal group riding.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their actual location and speed.

questions.question: Which of the following will help you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: Slow down and use both brakes on slippery surfaces. Avoid sudden moves. Follow tire tracks left by cars instead of riding in the center of the lane. Watch for hazards like oil spots and gravel.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually safest to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed straight within your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight across angled railroad tracks in your lane. Turning to hit the tracks at a right angle is dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: How should you pack a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load. Keep the load over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight shifts forward while braking, what can you do?

options.text: Use less pressure on the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, your front wheel has more grip. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders ride in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and stay farther back from other vehicles. Use the headlights of cars ahead of you to see the road better. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: The group takes up less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to be split up.
Riders get to their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders get to their destination faster in a close group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group uses less road space, is easier for others to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights or during passes. Speed is not affected by how close the group rides.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road behind you. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex ones.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Signals help riders communicate in a group. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Assume that any vehicle that can enter your path will do so.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to complete the pass quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane could encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: Is the oily strip in the center of a lane safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in the center of traffic lanes. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can often ride around it while staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign, and what color are its letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: Why should you avoid changing gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: You might speed up too much.
Other drivers will not expect you to change gears.
The rough surface makes shifting harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions. Choose the position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: On short trips close to home

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips close to home
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes to stop safely.
